tasks.task: Get the brief and align with the project lead
tasks.what: Understand the scope and the deliverable due date.
tasks.how:
Get the brief from the project lead and check it against the standard scope
Hold a kick-off call with the project lead: scope, deliverable due date.

tasks.task: Clarify the key questions with the client
tasks.what: Make sure the scope is clear before building anything. If not sure on any point, to be confirmed by the client.
tasks.how:
Is it a tribe project for devotees only (core fans and lovers) or devotees and prospects (values / territory based)?
How many countries? Do we need separate tribe ID cards per country (we usually don't, but worth asking)?
Is the tribe sourcing for women only, men only, or both? If both, is the territory sent by the brand genderless?
Do we need to use the client's template (e.g. the client)?
Do we have the brand / product values, or do we need to ask the client for them?
tasks.watch_out:
If the territory is not genderless, challenge the client on process and cost: one corpus for men and one for women costs more than one corpus for both.
We always need to receive either an oral brief or a document with the brand values.

tasks.task: Check what can be reused internally
tasks.what: Reuse what Semantiweb already did on the same category, client, brand or market.
tasks.how:
Is it a "standard" / "light" tribes sourcing (e.g. the client) or a more extensive one (e.g. a group with several brands)?
Did we already do a tribe sourcing for this category (makeup, fragrance men, fragrance women, etc.)?
Did we already do one for this client, brand, product, a competitor, or this country?
If yes, source it internally to identify what can be reused: corpus, facets, queries, tribe ID cards.

tasks.what: Make sure your time on the project is planned.
tasks.how:
Check your staffing on Float.
Validate it with the project lead.

tasks.what: Make sure you have everything to start.
tasks.how: Confirm you have the template and the Excel working file.
tasks.output: Template and Excel file at hand

tasks.what: Immerse yourself in the brand.
tasks.how:
Go to the brand website and social media accounts.
Ask ChatGPT for the latest brand news (buzz, bestsellers, pop-up stores).

tasks.what: Understand how a tribes study works and how the storytelling is adapted to each brand.
tasks.how: Read tribes studies we already delivered (see Slack channel communities-project).

tasks.what: Capture conversations around the brand territory. The query depends on the project type (see key question 0.2: devotees only, or devotees and prospects).
tasks.how:
Build the query from the brand territory: its values, its name, its products.
Devotees only (core fans and lovers), no values: a very simple query on the brand and its products.; Example :; [client query example removed]
Devotees and prospects (values / territory based): add a territory of values to the brand query.; Example (excerpt):; [client query example removed]
tasks.watch_out: The query is very broad, so it will bring uninteresting verbatims. Do not spend too much time cleaning it: the study is more quali than quanti.

tasks.what: Collect ratings & reviews from our internal database.
tasks.how: Run an extraction query directly in the Corpus Manager.; Example:; (year:("2026" OR "2024" OR "2025")) AND ((country:("USA")) AND (marque_label_all:("[brand]")))

tasks.what: Collect TikTok content + Collect the comments of the most commented TikTok videos with Export Comments.
tasks.how:
Either via Meltwater.
Or via our internal tool, using identified hashtags (brand hashtags, community hashtags and its values).; - For the manual crawl :
Check that the "Sorter For TikTok & Instagram" extension is installed on your computer.
On TikTok, search the brand / its products > Videos tab > sort by comments, descending > scroll down 10 times to refresh the data.
In your working sheet, list the 50 most commented videos: one column for the link, one for the number of comments.
In Export Comments, paste the video links and launch the export.

tasks.what: Collect Reddit content: very important for this type of study.
tasks.how: Depending on access: via our internal tool, Radarly or Meltwater.

tasks.what: Collect Instagram and Pinterest content.
tasks.how: Via Radarly or Meltwater.

tasks.what: Collect the brand's own posts and the comments they generate.
tasks.how:
Via Export Comments: crawl around 50 TikTok posts with more than 100 comments.
Via Radarly: run an author query to crawl the brand's posts (e.g. @[brand]).
tasks.output: Brand posts and comments crawl output

tasks.what: Identify the actors, celebrities or influencers who best embody the community.
tasks.how:
List the muses:
Spot them directly in the data.
Draw on your own knowledge of the community.
Browse TikTok or Instagram, searching for the community's values in the search bar.
Crawl their posts via Radarly with the query "author:".

tasks.what: Make non-English data readable and reliable for analysis.
tasks.how:
If a native speaker is available: they translate and check the data (slang, irony, cultural references).
Otherwise: translate via the Files tool (see Corpus Manager methodology), then have a native speaker check the verbatims selected for the deck.
tasks.watch_out: Keep the original verbatim next to its translation, and label translations clearly in the deck.

tasks.what: Your project lead sees what has been launched and where it stands.
tasks.how: Fill in the shared Excel file step by step.
tasks.output: Shared Excel file up to date

tasks.what: Make the data ready for analysis.
tasks.how: Load the data in the Corpus Manager (see Corpus Manager methodology).

tasks.what: Get a first understanding of the corpus and start collecting material.
tasks.how:
Ask Claude whether celebrities, restaurant names or brands come up repeatedly.
Take 2 hours to read the data and set aside relevant verbatims.
tasks.watch_out: Hashtags are key in this type of study: communities are often explicitly named through them.

tasks.what: Get first leads on the communities.
tasks.how: Run frequencies per platform and per year.

tasks.task: Read top commenter profiles on Instagram
tasks.what: Understand who the core fans and lovers are behind the brand’s comments.
tasks.how: Read the bio and content of the 25 profiles commenting the most on the brand

tasks.what: Indicate the audience's socio-demographic profile and centers of interest.
tasks.how: In HypeAuditor, generate the audience analysis of the brand accounts (beauty, fashion, all).; 6
tasks.watch_out: extract pdf report of the audiences for the brand account on Instagram and Tik Tok to get some ideas of top interests of the audience + demographics + key contributors / influencers about the brand.

tasks.what: Show the macro trends shaping the brand universe and the centers of interest communities gather around (e.g. "Macro trends shaping the [brand] universe", "Communities come together around centers of interest").
tasks.how:
Identify them with the frequencies and desk research, then confirm them in the corpus.
Use the search bar: is there enough volume to support the idea?
To quantify: queries.
tasks.output: Incarnation and centers of interest slides

tasks.what: Find the common thread of these communities.
tasks.how: Define it with the project lead.

tasks.what: Define and name the tribes.
tasks.how:
Brainstorm with the project lead.
Ask ChatGPT for naming ideas.
Look at the Pinterest trend report of the current year: often very inspiring in terms of insights.
If planned upstream, send the communities to the client for validation (check with the project lead).

tasks.what: One ID card per community.
tasks.how:
Run frequencies per community, previously quantified with semantic queries.
Who are they, centers of interest.
Key temples.
Pillars: qualitative, perception of the community and of the brand.
tasks.watch_out: Tip: identify a content creator who embodies the community and browse their profile to see what they do, where they go, etc.

tasks.what: Illustrate each community.
tasks.how:
Take visuals on Pinterest (more qualitative).
Add an influencer example who embodies the community: find them through your own knowledge, ChatGPT, HypeAuditor or Traackr.
tasks.watch_out: Choose visuals that are not blurry: it is the first thing a client sees.

tasks.what: Summarize the pillars across communities.
tasks.how: Ask Claude to do it.

tasks.what: Help the client choose which communities to activate.
tasks.how: Brainstorm with the project lead.

tasks.what: don't forget the ending slide with your name + project lead
The deck is clean and client-ready.
tasks.how:
No duplicate verbatims.
Base 100 adds up to 100.
Same font everywhere.
Title = insight.
No comments or notes left at the bottom of the slides.
Good quality photos.

tasks.what: Keep the project team aligned throughout the study.
tasks.how: Plan at least 2 to 3 review calls per week with the project team.

tasks.what: Anticipate the restitution.
tasks.how:
Confirm with the project lead whether you should attend.
Make sure you have the invitation.

tasks.what: Get feedback on your work.
tasks.how: After the restitution, ask the project lead for written feedback (plus a quick coffee or call if needed).

deck.title: Tribes Study | Deck Structure
deck.description: Standard slide sequence of a tribes (community) study deck, with the data each slide needs and when it is included.
rows: Brand, market, date; agenda with section numbers.
3 steps: data sourcing and extraction (platforms), structuration via LLM/NLP, quanti + quali analysis.
Query extract, conversation volume per market, owned accounts follower analysis; number of communities mapped.
Brand query, corpus volume, follower data (HypeAuditor)
Always (follower analysis if owned accounts in scope)
Core fans vs lovers definition, each with a one-line consumer stance.
Headline; 4 to 5 bullets on relationship to the brand; takeaway; 2 to 3 verbatims; visuals.
Pyramid: core fans (advocacy) vs lovers (conversion), definition and opportunity per level.
3 aspirations on the brand territory, one visual each.
Trend description, why the brand, 1 verbatim, moodboard.
5 to 6 interests ranked with % and top sub-themes, visual each.
One overarching consumer shift the brand world resonates with, 3 supporting points.
All communities with share, evolution arrow, visual; 4 to 5 reading bullets on the ecosystem.
AI-generated or brief tribes vs sourced communities; mapping of echoes.
Pyramid with share of fans vs lovers and community count; communities placed by type with share.

Type tag, share + evolution, tagline; brand pillars score; socio-demo (generation slider, male audience); top words & hashtags; who are they; 4 centers of interest; key temples incl. platform split base 100; echo of hypothesis tribe.
Community facets, profiles, top words, platforms
Always (hypothesis echo if tribes generated upstream)
Handle, followers, ER, portrait, 2 post verbatims, feed visuals.
All communities with share, evolution and brand pillar scores side by side.
Communities split ownable (dominant & growing) vs tactical (niche & rising), ranked, one rationale each.
